entries.title: Russian strike on buses kills at least 30, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge
entries.snippet: Ukraine accused Russia of targeting the crowded bus in the frontline city to kill as many civilians as possible.

entries.title: US and Lebanon protecting wanted Syrian general, BBC finds
entries.snippet: Bassam al-Hassan is being sheltered in return for information - including about abducted US reporter Austin Tice.

entries.title: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain
entries.snippet: Israel said in September it would act in response to UK sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

entries.title: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
entries.snippet: A lawyer says the murderer of Colleen Slemmer is moving around her hospital room after surviving two lethal injections.

entries.title: Italy overhauls electoral system after fiercely contested debate
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says the move will deliver more stable government, but opposition parties say her aim is to stay in power.

entries.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
entries.snippet: Casualties have been reported on the vessel, identified by a maritime intelligence firm as the oil and chemical tanker, Acers.

entries.title: Outspoken Indian actor Nana Patekar suddenly dies at 75
entries.snippet: Known for his intense performances, Patekar carved out a distinctive place in Indian cinema.

entries.title: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
entries.snippet: The Mapocho river has burst its banks after an unusually large amount of rain fell in recent days.

entries.title: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
entries.snippet: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years in September.

entries.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine envoy over prisoner-of-war row
entries.snippet: It is the latest in a diplomatic spat after Kyiv disclosed that two North Korean prisoners were transferred to Seoul.

entries.title: France's school protests: What lies behind the anger
entries.snippet: Students' blockades and marches spring from real grievances – and from France's habit of settling policy on the street.

entries.title: Bear kills man in home attack near Mongolian capital
entries.snippet: Police say the bear entered a traditional nomadic dwelling near Ulaanbaatar, killing a man and seriously injured a woman.

entries.title: Texas carries out first US execution since Christa Pike's botched lethal injections
entries.snippet: Lawyers for Jamaal Howard had asked a judge to pause the execution after Christa Pike's botched lethal injections.

entries.title: New York court hears arguments in ongoing 9/11 families' lawsuit against Saudi Arabia
entries.snippet: The families allege that men with links to the Saudi government helped those who carried out the 2001 attacks, something the country denies.

entries.title: Eritrean troops move deep into Ethiopia's Tigray region, residents tell BBC
entries.snippet: Residents of Adigrat tell the BBC they have seen truck loads of soldiers from Eritrea moving south.

entries.title: Margaret Hamilton, whose software helped land Apollo 11 on the Moon, dies at 90
entries.snippet: Pioneering computer scientist led the development of the software for Nasa's Apollo mission and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

entries.title: Trump wants a new Camp David-like retreat at his Florida golf club
entries.snippet: Trump's estate would stand in stark contrast to the rustic Camp David and mark another tradition transformed by Trump.

entries.title: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro expected to face more charges this week
entries.snippet: The new charges are expected to accuse Maduro and his wife of playing a role in the torture of Americans in Venezuelan prisons, US media reports.

entries.title: Asahi and Kirin among Japan beer giants raided over alleged price-fixing cartel
entries.snippet: Japan's Fair Trade Commission conducted searches of the country's largest beer-makers.

entries.title: Three people killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia airports, officials say
entries.snippet: The Houthis have claimed responsibility for the attacks, which mark an escalation in the conflict.

entries.title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW dispute
entries.snippet: The South Korean announcement on Thursday came days after its President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified punitive steps if Ukraine refuses to apologize over the revelation.

entries.title: South Korea test-flies its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon
entries.snippet: The test follows North Korea's recent hypersonic missile test. Tensions between the Koreas have increased after land mine explosions injured three South Korean soldiers near the border. North Korea denies responsibility.

entries.title: Isaias intensifies to hurricane. And, judge orders Pike execution evidence preserved
entries.snippet: People in the Gulf are preparing for bad weather this weekend after Isaias intensified into a hurricane. And, a judge has ordered Christa Pike's failed execution evidence be preserved.

entries.title: Strike on Ukrainian public bus leaves 30 dead as blackouts worsen in Kyiv
entries.snippet: Russian strikes in eastern Ukraine have killed 30 people and injured at least 18, according to authorities. The attacks included a strike on a public bus and have worsened power outages in Kyiv.

entries.title: ICE has quietly used this warehouse as a detention facility all summer, neighbors say
entries.snippet: Throughout the summer, rumors have been bubbling in North New Jersey that ICE has quietly been using a warehouse as a detention center. NPR investigated.

entries.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
entries.snippet: In Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous, a new system could screen hospital patients for financial aid, preventing hundreds of thousands from getting bills they can't pay.

entries.title: Syrian general accused of atrocities is protected by U.S. and Lebanon, NPR and BBC find
entries.snippet: A former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity is living quietly in Lebanon, bankrolled and protected by American and Lebanese authorities, a BBC/NPR investigation has found.

entries.title: As crypto and prediction markets expand, their regulator shrinks
entries.snippet: Even as the agency is tasked with drawing up new rules for crypto and prediction markets, its staffing and enforcement actions have dropped precipitously during the second Trump administration.

entries.title: Toss-ups, triage and targets: How to read the wide-open 2026 House map
entries.snippet: Both parties are spending heavily in roughly 60 House districts — where Trump won by an average of nine points in 2024 — that could be key to deciding control of the chamber, an NPR analysis finds.

entries.title: Flock is catching flak. Experts say other police surveillance tools are more worrisome
entries.snippet: Real-time crime-center software is a sometimes overlooked but powerful tool allowing police to aggregate immense amounts of data, significantly expanding their surveillance reach.

entries.title: Student loan borrowers have more time to reduce interest rates. Here's what to know
entries.snippet: The original deadline was Sept. 30, but the U.S. Department of Education extended it to give borrowers more time to enroll. The rate reduction will last through June 2028.

entries.title: Eva Marie Saint, star of 'On the Waterfront' and 'North by Northwest,' dies at 102
entries.snippet: Saint had one of the most spectacular debuts in Hollywood history, as the love interest of Marlon Brando's tormented Terry Malloy in "On the Waterfront."

entries.title: What the Cornell case reveals about how sexual assault allegations are handled

entries.title: Why French students are leading massive protests across the country
entries.snippet: Protests are continuing in France, a day after more than 250,000 people took to the streets across the country to demand education reforms. Demonstrations began in mid-September, fueled by frustrations over classroom sizes and poor building conditions. Special correspondent Willi

entries.snippet: A growing body of evidence suggests that GLP-1 drugs are not only helping millions with their diabetes and weight loss, but they're also proving effective at curbing people's desire for drugs and alcohol. William Brangham reports on the researchers who are testing whether these m

entries.snippet: Israel is marking the third anniversary of one of its darkest days. On Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas terrorists stormed Israeli communities, killing 1,200 people and kidnapping 251 more. Nick Schifrin reports on one survivor and his determination to create, out of the horrors, a new genera

entries.snippet: Three years after Oct. 7, two fathers are reaching across the gulf that divides Israelis and Palestinians. Jonathan Dekel-Chen is the father of Sagui Dekel-Chen, who was shot, kidnapped and held hostage for nearly 500 days. Jaser Abu Moussa is from Gaza and an Israeli airstrike k

entries.title: Tropical storm threat churns planning for Georgia-Alabama game with Trump set to attend
entries.snippet: Tropical Storm Isaias could make landfall on the U.S. Gulf Coast as a hurricane this weekend, hours before No. 2 Georgia plays at No. 6 Alabama in a major college football game on Saturday night that President Donald Trump is planning to attend.

entries.title: Trump's $90 Medicare rebate rolls out, but millions aren't eligible. Critics see a political stunt
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump says his administration will make one-time payments of $90 per person to help more than 20 million Medicare enrollees pay for their Part B premiums. It will cost about $2 billion.

entries.title: WATCH: Canadian writer Anne Carson wins Nobel Prize in literature
entries.snippet: Toronto-born Carson, 76, draws on themes and stories from ancient Greek and Roman literature for works that often blend elements of poetry, essay and fiction.

entries.title: Flight attendants' union raises safety concerns over Trump's Washington arch
entries.snippet: The union representing thousands of flight attendants said Wednesday it has safety concerns about President Donald Trump's proposed triumphal arch that will be on final approach to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.

entries.title: Trump's executive order on dyed diesel will offer little relief, farmers and truckers say
entries.snippet: Farmers, truckers and economists say a move to cut taxes on diesel will provide little relief from record-high fuel prices that have soared since the U.S. attacked Iran months ago.

entries.title: WATCH: Rubio urges Europe to defend Western values and strengthen U.S. alliance in Greece
entries.snippet: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in a sweeping speech against the backdrop of the Acropolis in Athens, called for the nations of the West to return to their civilizational roots and restore the values that drove the rise of Europe and North America to global dominance for centurie

entries.title: Trump administration proposes a $70,000 fee for international students to work in the U.S.
entries.snippet: The Department of Homeland Security on Wednesday proposed a $70,000 fee for international students seeking to work in the United States, the latest effort from the Trump administration to crack down on foreign enrollment.

entries.title: DNC files lawsuit alleging Trump's taxpayer-funded ads are illegal propaganda
entries.snippet: The Democratic National Committee on Wednesday sued President Donald Trump's administration for recent television advertisements that promoted his political message while costing taxpayers millions of dollars.

entries.title: FBI says it stopped a Mall of America terror attack by a teen after agents sold him an assault rifle
entries.snippet: FBI agents thwarted a terror attack by a teenager on the Mall of America after monitoring him for nearly two years and ultimately supplying him with the assault rifle he planned to use, authorities said Wednesday.

entries.title: Shock gloves purchased by ICE cause pain, compliance and fear, Army study found
entries.snippet: The shock gloves immigration agents could soon use to control detainees and protesters worked so powerfully during a military exercise that participants felt intense pain, stopped fighting immediately and feared additional exposures, according to a previously unreleased Army stud

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: India news: Opposition doubles down against poll chief after detentions
entries.snippet: India's opposition alliance is gearing up for another day of protests after demonstrating lawmakers were detained for the second time. Meanwhile, India is seeking to repatriate its nationals working in Russian military.

entries.title: Security in the Black Sea region: is Bulgaria the weak link in Europe's defense against threats from Russia?
entries.snippet: Two ships have sunk off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Sofia has held back on pointing the finger at Russia. What does that mean for security in the Black Sea and the region?

entries.title: French police arrest 5 suspects over Renoir museum theft
entries.snippet: Thieves broke into the Renoir Museum on the French Riviera last month and made off with two paintings. The heist follows a string of high-profile robberies from European museums.

entries.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
entries.snippet: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

entries.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
entries.snippet: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

entries.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine ambassador amid POW dispute
entries.snippet: South Korea has said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul is upset about a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war being made public knowledge at the UN and had demanded — but not received — an apology.

entries.title: As Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian data centers, could Ukraine soon be offline?
entries.snippet: As Russia targets Ukraine's data centers more and more, experts say the country's internet system is too robust to shut down entirely. However, services could become more expensive.

entries.title: Ukraine says 30 killed, 18 wounded in Russian attack on passenger buses in Kramatorsk
entries.snippet: Authorities in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk have suspended public transport following the deadly attack near the front line.

entries.title: UK scales back Jerusalem consulate after Israel dispute
entries.snippet: Britain says its diplomatic mission will remain open with reduced staff, despite Israel's order to close the nearly 200-year-old consulate.

entries.title: German Bundeswehr: A new naval port in Emden aims to enhance Germany's defense capabilities
entries.snippet: Citing the escalating security threat, Germany's Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast. Emden was chosen as the location.

entries.title: NASA Apollo program pioneer Margaret Hamilton dies
entries.snippet: US scientist Margaret Hamilton is being hailed as a pioneer for her groundbreaking work developing software for NASA's Apollo lunar program. She died at the age of 90.

entries.title: Middle Corridor: Can Bulgaria be a safe gateway for Asian imports to the EU?
entries.snippet: The EU wants more trade via the Middle Corridor, which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. But Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast are a stark reminder of the security risks involved.

entries.title: US to lay fresh torture charges against Venezuela's Maduro and wife
entries.snippet: Prosecutors are considering charges for the alleged torture of more than a dozen Americans detained in Venezuela. Meanwhile, Cilia Flores is seeking release from jail on health grounds.

entries.title: Germany news: UK's Burnham, Merz to talk security in Berlin
entries.snippet: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is visiting Berlin to launch a joint security partnership with Germany. President Steinmeier is on a state visit to France. DW has more.

entries.title: Yemen's Houthis claim strike on Riyadh airport, three killed
entries.snippet: A Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed three people and disrupted operations, the rebels said, as Yemen's conflict continues to escalate beyond its borders.

entries.title: Why music in Iran is more than just entertainment
entries.snippet: Iranian authorities are trying to persuade prominent singers in exile to return home. While the state seeks to harness music as a political tool, music has also become a powerful expression of dissent and resistance.

entries.title: South Sudan's road to elections remains uncertain
entries.snippet: South Sudan's first general election is set for December 22. Insecurity, political tensions and the failure to begin voter registration have raised doubts over whether a credible poll can be held.

entries.title: US: Award-winning Kashmiri filmmaker detained
entries.snippet: Arfat Sheikh was detained by ICE agents in Washington on September 24, it was confirmed on Wednesday. Officials say he "illegally overstayed his lawful admittance" as US President Trump pursues an immigration clampdown.

entries.title: IMF reaches tentative $1.21 billion bailout deal with Pakistan
entries.snippet: Pakistan's dependence on Gulf energy imports, remittances and regional financing has left the economy exposed to the fallout from the Middle East conflict.
